title: How Hydration Supports Weight Health and Everyday Functioning

authorship.current_visible_author: Healthy Weight Literacy Foundation Editorial Team
authorship.recommended_normalized_author: Healthy Weight Literacy Foundation Editorial Team

primary_question: How does hydration affect weight health specifically, and how much water do I need?
reader_intent: Understand the specific mechanisms by which hydration may support weight management.
desired_reader_outcome: Reader understands general hydration needs and several specific weight-management-adjacent hydration mechanisms.

claims.proposition: One study found that people who drank water before meals ate fewer calories than those who didn't.
claims.recommended_action: Names an unidentified 'one study' with zero citation — a real, checkable claim (this describes a genuine, identifiable line of research, most commonly a Davy et al.-type pre-meal water study) is currently presented as if from memory. Identify and cite the actual specific study before restating this claim.

claims.proposition: Drinking cold water may slightly boost metabolism as the body expends energy to warm it to body temperature.
claims.recommended_action: Appropriately hedged as a small, non-primary effect; still uncited.

claims.proposition: The National Academies recommends approximately 3.7 liters (men) / 2.7 liters (women) of total fluids per day.
claims.article_location: "How Much Water Do You Need?" section

internal_link_recommendations.reason: Nearly identical reader job; should be consulted together until merged.

disposition_reason: This reader job (how much water do I need, plus weight-management hydration mechanisms) is almost entirely duplicated by hydration-and-health-how-much-water-do-you-need, which covers the same NASEM figures and myth-debunking more rigorously. This article's genuinely distinct content — the thirst-vs-hunger reframe and the specific 'water before meals' claim (once properly sourced) — is worth preserving by folding into the survivor rather than maintaining two near-identical URLs.
required_research: Identify and cite the actual specific study behind the 'water before meals reduces calorie intake' claim before it is carried into the merged article.
recommended_rewrite_scope: Fold the thirst-vs-hunger and pre-meal-water content into hydration-and-health-how-much-water-do-you-need as a properly sourced subsection, then redirect this URL.
